transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, doctor. Well, I guess I came in because my eating has just gotten all turned around. It's been going on for months now. 

Some days I barely eat... I just pick at a piece of toast and have some coffee. But then other days, I'll find myself just standing in the bakery aisle at the grocery store, buying a bunch of sweets that I don't even really enjoy eating. It's just strange, and I wanted to see what's going on.
After you eat those sweets or larger amounts of food, do you do anything to try to compensate or make up for it — like making yourself vomit, exercising excessively, or using laxatives?

No, I don't do any of that. I just... well, I just eat them and then I usually sit there feeling kind of bad about it. But I've never made myself throw up or taken laxatives or anything like that. And I definitely don't exercise to make up for it.
When you're not eating much or when you're eating those sweets and feeling bad about it afterward, how is your overall mood? Do you feel sad, empty, or down most of the time?

Yes, I do feel down most of the time. Actually, most days I wake up with this heavy, sad feeling just... sitting on me. It's hard to explain, but even when I'm standing in my bright kitchen with the coffee going in the morning, I just feel like the warmth has gone out of everything. So, yes, I'm definitely feeling very sad lately.

Besides the eating and your mood, are there other things you normally enjoy doing — like hobbies, time with friends, or activities you used to like — that just don't feel enjoyable or interesting to you anymore?

Yes, I've noticed that too. I used to really get excited about things like my quilting squares, or going to bowling night... and I always liked planning potlucks. But lately, I'll just look at my sewing supplies sitting there, or look at the church calendar, and I just can't make myself care the way I used to. I just don't have any interest in them right now.
You mentioned feeling this heavy, sad feeling most days — how long has this been going on? Can you remember roughly when it started?
Well, it's been going on for... I guess about seven months now. It started right around the time my aunt came to live with me, just after she had her fall.
How has your sleep been during these past seven months? Are you sleeping more than usual, less than usual, or about the same?

My sleep? Um, I think it's been about the same, really. I haven't noticed myself sleeping a whole lot more, or... or less than I usually do. I just go to bed and wake up at my normal times, for the most part.
Before these past seven months, have you ever had a period lasting at least two weeks where you felt this same kind of sadness, loss of interest in things, or depression?
No, I don't think so. I mean, I've had sad days before, like anyone else, but never anything that lasted for weeks like this... or felt this heavy. This is the first time it's been this bad.
During these past seven months, have you noticed changes in your energy level — like feeling more tired or fatigued than usual, even when you're resting?

Yeah, I have noticed that. Even after a full night of sleep, you know, on the nights when my aunt doesn't call out for me, I still feel completely worn down by the time breakfast rolls around. It's like just doing normal things... carrying the laundry or making a few phone calls... it just takes way more out of me than it should.

Have you ever had a period — even a few days or a week — where your mood was unusually high or 'up,' where you felt more energetic than normal, or where you needed much less sleep than usual but still felt rested and full of energy?
No, I haven't ever felt like that. I don't think I've ever had a time where I felt unusually high or energetic. I mean, I have good days sometimes, but nothing extreme, and I always need my sleep.

During these past seven months when you've been feeling this sadness and heaviness, have you ever heard voices or seen things that other people around you couldn't hear or see, or have you had beliefs that felt absolutely true to you even though others didn't agree with them?

Yes, I have. A few times a week, especially when the house gets quiet after my aunt goes to sleep, I hear my name. Or sometimes it's a voice telling me that I ruined everything. It sounds so clear, just as if someone were standing right there in the kitchen with me... but when I look, there is never anyone there.

When you hear your name or the voice telling you that you ruined everything, do you believe that voice is real — like an actual person speaking to you — or do you know it's coming from inside your mind?

I'm not really sure, honestly. When it happens, it sounds completely real... like an actual person is right there speaking to me. But since I know nobody else is in the room, I just... I don't really know what to think. I guess I'm not sure if it's coming from inside my mind or not, because it just sounds so real in the moment.

Before these past seven months, have you ever had another time in your life — even years ago — when you felt depressed or down for several weeks or longer, or when you lost interest in things you normally enjoyed?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I've had normal ups and downs over the years, like anybody else. But nothing like this... I've never felt this down or just completely uninterested in everything for weeks at a time before this started seven months ago.
